Tonmya.text: In August 2025, we received approval from the FDA for TONMYA® (cyclobenzaprine HCl sublingual tablets) for the treatment of fibromyalgia. TONMYA, our first internally developed product to become FDA approved, was commercially launched by us in the United States on November 17, 2025. TONMYA is the first new medicine for fibromyalgia in more than 15 years and is a centrally acting, non-opioid analgesic designed for bedtime administration and long-term use. We hold worldwide commercialization rights to TONMYA. In addition to TONMYA, we market two FDA-approved prescription products for the treatment of acute migraine: Zembrace® SymTouch® (sumatriptan injection) and Tosymra® (sumatriptan nasal spray). Our commercial platform includes sales, marketing, market access, distribution, and patient support capabilities. We are advancing a diversified development pipeline generated through internal discovery, in-licensing, acquisitions, and collaborations with academic and non-profit institutions. Our pipeline addresses conditions that span CNS, infectious disease, immunology, and rare disease, with multiple programs in clinical and preclinical development. TONMYA’s proprietary cyclobenzaprine HCl sublingual tablet formulation is referred to as “TNX-102 SL” outside of the fibromyalgia indication.

Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $45.6 million, an increase of $19.9 million, or 77% from $25.7 million incurred in the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is primarily due to an increase in sales and marketing expenses of $13.5 million, employee-related expenses of $4.1 million, and professional expenses of $1.5 million. These increases primarily reflect commercialization activities following the launch of TONMYA in November 2025.

prov.text: In July 2025, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (the “FASB”) issued Accounting Standards Update (“ASU”) 2025-05, Financial Instruments—Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets , which provides guidance for estimating credit losses under the current expected credit losses (CECL) model for current accounts receivable and current contract assets arising from transactions accounted for under Accounting Standards Codification 606. We have adopted this ASU on a prospective basis, and it did not have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.

net.text: Net Loss . As a result of the foregoing, the net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $53.3 million, an increase of $21.3 million, or 66.6%, compared to a net loss of $32.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

ocf.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, we used approximately $125.6 million and $60.2 million of cash in operating activities, respectively, which represents cash outlays for research and development and general and administrative expenses in such periods. The increase in cash outlays principally resulted from an increase in research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses. Cash used in investing activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $2.9 million related to the purchase of property and equipment. Cash used in investing activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, was $3.5 million related to the issuance of a note and purchase of property and equipment. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, net cash provided from financing activities was $82.0 million and $155.4 million, respectively, predominantly from the issuance of common stock.

sbc.text: Stock-based compensation expense related to options was $2.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, including $1.7 million in selling, general and administrative expenses and $0.5 million in research and development expenses. Stock-based compensation expense related to options was $1.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, including $1.2 million in selling, general and administrative expenses and $0.6 million in research and development expenses.

wc.text: As of September 30, 2026, we had working capital of $150.1 million, comprised primarily of cash and cash equivalents of $162.8 million, accounts receivable, net of $14.6 million, inventory of $4.5 million and prepaid expenses and other current assets of $10.3 million, offset by $17.1 million of accounts payable, $24.6 million of accrued expenses, and current lease liabilities of $0.3 million. A significant portion of the accounts payable and accrued expenses is due to work performed in relation to our clinical programs, accruals for gross to net deductions related to our commercial products and launch of TONMYA.

Tonmya.text: TONMYA® (cyclobenzaprine HCl sublingual tablets 2.8 mg), our flagship internally conceived and developed medicine, is the first new medicine for fibromyalgia in adults approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) in more than 15 years. Our CNS commercial infrastructure supports our marketed products, including our acute migraine products, Zembrace® SymTouch® (sumatriptan injection 3 mg) and Tosymra® (sumatriptan nasal spray 10 mg). We received approval from the FDA for TONMYA for the treatment of fibromyalgia in adults in August 2025 and commercially launched TONMYA in November 2025. TONMYA is a centrally acting, non-opioid analgesic designed for bedtime administration and long-term use, for which we hold worldwide commercialization rights. Our commercial platform includes sales, marketing, market access, distribution, and patient support capabilities.

intro.text: Tonix Pharmaceuticals (“Tonix” or the “Company”) is a fully-integrated biopharmaceutical company commercializing and developing innovative therapies for central nervous system (“CNS”) disorders, infectious diseases, immunology, and rare diseases. Our portfolio consists of both commercial and development-stage programs. Tonix markets TONMYA® (cyclobenzaprine HCl sublingual tablets) for the treatment of fibromyalgia in adults in the U.S., as well as Zembrace® SymTouch® (sumatriptan injection) and Tosymra® (sumatriptan nasal spray) for the treatment of acute migraine in adults in the U.S. Tonix received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) for TONMYA for the treatment of fibromyalgia in August 2025 and commercially launched TONMYA in November 2025.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
